questions.q: Who is the author of "फुलचंद की एकवह" and what is his primary literary identity?
questions.a: Correct answer: Upendranath Ashk (उपेन्द्रनाथ अश्क), a prominent Hindi writer known for short stories, novels, and autobiographical sketches. A wrong answer (e.g., naming Premchand or guessing a poet) reveals the student has not read the author blurb or linked the chapter to the writer’s name — a basic recall gap that will hinder later analysis of authorial voice.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what an "आत्मकथात्मक रेखाचित्र" (autobiographical sketch) is and how it differs from a full autobiography.
questions.a: Correct answer: An autobiographical sketch is a short, focused literary piece that captures a specific memory, person, or episode from the writer’s life with artistic shaping — unlike a full autobiography which covers the entire life chronologically. A wrong answer that equates it with a diary entry or a biography shows the student misses the literary craft (selection, emphasis, thematic unity) central to the genre.

questions.q: Based on the introductory note, list three concrete details about the rural setting (time, place, occupation) that you expect to encounter in the chapter.
questions.a: Correct answer: (1) Early 20th‑century Punjab village, (2) Pottery‑making (कुम्हार/देय) as a central occupation, (3) Seasonal cycles (monsoon, harvest) shaping daily life. A wrong answer that gives generic "village life" without specifics indicates the student skimmed the background note and cannot anchor later textual evidence.

questions.q: Compare the mother‑child relationship hinted at in the background note with a similar relationship in another Hindi text you studied in Class 11 (e.g., "गिल्लू" or "नमक का दारोगा"). What thematic parallel do you anticipate?
questions.a: Correct answer: Both depict a nurturing, protective mother figure whose love is expressed through small acts (feeding, guarding) and whose loss creates an emotional void — a recurring theme in Hindi autobiographical writing. A wrong answer that only describes plot events without linking to the universal theme of maternal love shows inability to transfer thematic understanding across texts.

questions.q: Evaluate: "Knowing the author’s life history is more important than understanding the genre conventions for appreciating this chapter." Defend your position with two reasons.
questions.a: Correct evaluation: Disagree. Genre conventions (e.g., selective memory, artistic shaping in रेखाचित्र) dictate how the author transforms life into art; ignoring them leads to reading the text as mere factual record. Also, the text’s emotional impact comes from literary devices (imagery, symbolism) that belong to craft, not biography. A wrong answer that prioritizes biography alone reveals a naive "life = text" fallacy common in board exams.

questions.q: Create a 4‑line poetic snapshot (in Hindi or English) that captures the atmosphere of a potter’s village at dawn, using at least two sensory images suggested by the background note.
questions.a: Good answer example: "भोर की धुंध में चाक की धुन / मिट्टी की सौंधी गंध उड़ती / फुलचंद के हाथों आकार लेती / एक और एकवह, चुपचाप।" A poor answer that merely states "potter makes pots" without sensory imagery shows the student cannot translate contextual clues into creative evocation — a skill needed for literary appreciation questions.
